sixtySeconds.whatItDoes: DeepTutor is a personal AI tutoring workspace from HKU's Data Intelligence Lab. It brings chat, quizzes, research, reading, practice and learning paths together in one app, grounded in your own documents, and remembers what you have learned.
sixtySeconds.problem: Studying with a plain chatbot loses track of your materials and progress. DeepTutor keeps your books, documents and notes in libraries it cites from, tracks mastery, and adapts tutoring over time with memory you can inspect.
whoFor: Researchers working through papers and books
Self-hosters who want a private learning app
sixtySeconds.whyChoose: Choose it for an all-in-one, open-source learning workspace with many study modes, source-linked answers and transparent memory, installable as a desktop app, Docker container or Python package.
requirements: Docker, or Python 3.11 to 3.14 with Node.js 20.9+ for the full web app
An LLM provider (set during deeptutor init)

overview: DeepTutor has many learning modes sharing one context: Chat, Quiz, Research, Visualize, Solve, Mastery Path and Reading. Home, Learning and Resources tie together Books, Practice, a Task Board, a Calendar and a learning notebook.

You build knowledge libraries with LlamaIndex, PageIndex, GraphRAG or LightRAG and learn next to documents, video and audio with citations. Memory works in levels (traces, facts, synthesis) and can be inspected in a Memory Graph. It can also consult agents such as Claude Code, Codex and Grok CLI.

Install options: a preview desktop app for macOS and Windows, a Docker image, a PyPI package (deeptutor[full] for the web app and CLI, plain deeptutor for core chat and the SDK), or a source checkout. It is Apache 2.0 licensed.
